title: Protocol-relative CSS URLs bypassed remote asset detection

examples: CSS hex escapes such as url(\2f \2f collector.invalid/pixel)
reproduction.beforeFix: The gate's CSS URL pattern required an explicit http or https scheme and returned pass for protocol-relative image and font URLs, including CSS-escaped slashes.
reproduction.afterFix: CSS resource scanning normalizes simple/hex escapes and recognizes explicit http/https URLs and scheme-relative // URLs. The existing URL-constructor exclusion remains in place.

rootCause: The lexical CSS resource matcher only accepted the `http://` or `https://` prefix even though browsers resolve `//host/path` as a network request using the current scheme.
remediation: Normalize CSS simple/hex escapes before matching scheme-relative URLs, while retaining the separate handling for JavaScript URL constructor text.
